newsitem.title: UK: Britons throw off inhibitions for Valentine's Day.
newsitem.headline: Britons throw off inhibitions for Valentine's Day.

text.p: British lovers, would-be lovers and pure romantics threw off their inhibitions on Friday, celebrating Valentine's Day by filling newspapers with page upon page of ardent, amusing and toe-curling messages.

Cuddly Bear, Sexy Bum, Cheddar Chops and Rambo unsheathed their metaphors and double-entendres in the Sun tabloid. The Times preferred first names but Stallion and Tigerbunny professed their desires for the whole world to see.

Streaky asked Val to marry him, Chochy told Plop that he loved her -- or she loved him -- more than life itself and Boldheart informed Susan she was pure gold and that every one of her carats was pure perfection.

Down at the other end of the market, A told Stinky to "get em off". Angie was told that Ray still liked her wobbly bits and Arkwright suggested to Gladys Emmanuelle that they act like steam trains and "let's couple and shunt forever".
Superman and Lois Lane, Pooh and Piglet, and Ulysses all displayed their love and, with an election only weeks away, politics also entered the fray.
Cosmopolitan magazine asked Prime Minister John Major and opposition leader Tony Blair what was the most significant event in their lives.
Blair said becoming Labour party leader, probably true but his wife Cherie would secretly prefer Major's reply.

"Marrying Norma is the single most significant event of my life. I was married to Norma long before I became prime minister. I will be married to Norma long after I cease to be prime minister," Major said.
Cuddly Carp, Swiggley Diddley and Scrubby Widget would probably greet that sentiment with a dreamy "Aaaaaaaaah".
